name: Artificial intelligence (AI)
definition: Software that can do tasks we used to think needed a human, like writing, summarising or recognising a picture. It is not alive and not thinking; it is a very capable tool.

name: Generative AI
definition: AI that makes new content, words, images, audio or code, rather than just sorting or finding things. The chat tools you have heard of are generative AI.

name: Large language model (LLM)
definition: The engine inside chat tools like ChatGPT and Claude. It is a system that has read an enormous amount of writing and is very good at predicting what words should come next. That prediction is how it talks with you.

name: Prompt
definition: What you type to an AI. Your instruction or question. A clear, specific prompt gets a far more useful answer than a vague one.

name: Token
definition: The small chunks of text an LLM reads and writes, roughly a word or part of a word. Tools count usage and length in tokens. You almost never need to think about them.

name: Hallucination
definition: When AI states something false in the same confident, fluent tone it uses when it is right. It is not lying; it predicted what sounded right. This is why you verify any fact before relying on it.

name: Training data
definition: The huge collection of text and other content an AI learned from. Most tools learned up to a certain date, which is why they can be wrong about very recent events.

name: Model
definition: A single AI system, like a specific version of ChatGPT or Claude. New models are released regularly, usually a bit more capable than the last.

name: Context window
definition: How much an AI can hold in mind at once in a conversation, including what you have said and what it has replied. Very long chats can push earlier details out of view.

name: Machine learning
definition: The broader field of teaching software to find patterns from examples rather than being given fixed rules. LLMs are one kind of machine learning.

name: Multimodal
definition: An AI that can work with more than just text, for example reading an image you upload, or listening to your voice. Most leading tools are now multimodal.

name: AI agent
definition: An AI set up to take steps on its own toward a goal, such as booking or filling something in, rather than only answering. Useful, but it deserves closer supervision.

name: Inference
definition: The moment an AI produces an answer from your prompt. When people say a tool is "thinking", this is what is happening.

name: Fine-tuning
definition: Taking a general model and training it a little more on specific material so it is better at a particular job or style.

name: Bias
definition: When an AI reflects unfair patterns from its training data, for example treating some groups or topics differently. A reason to keep a human checking important decisions.

name: Deepfake
definition: A fake image, video or voice made by AI to look or sound like a real person. The reason a family code word and a second check on any money request now matter.

name: Guardrails
definition: The limits a company builds into an AI to stop it doing harmful things. Helpful, but not perfect, so your own judgement still matters.

name: API
definition: A way for one piece of software to talk to another. It is how apps connect to an AI behind the scenes. A term you will see but rarely need.

name: Open weight (open source) model
definition: A model whose inner workings are released publicly so anyone can run or build on it, as opposed to one only used through a company’s app.

name: Prompt engineering
definition: A grand name for the simple skill of writing clear instructions to an AI: giving it context, a role, the format you want, and refining from there.
